text: Working with APIs is a valuable skill for modern developers. An API allows different software applications to communicate with each other. When you interact with an API, you typically make HTTP requests to a server, such as GET to retrieve data or POST to send new information. The server often responds with JSON, a lightweight data format that is easy for both humans and machines to read. Most APIs require authentication, usually with an API key, to ensure that only authorized users can access the service. It’s also important to be aware of rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a given time period. Finally, always implement proper error handling to manage problems like network failures or invalid responses gracefully, as these are inevitable in real-world applications.
